title: fix(metadata): one owner for idx_sys_metadata_overlay_active — remove the stale-keyed second producer
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#6771

`idx_sys_metadata_overlay_active` had **two** producers with **different** keys, both
issuing `CREATE ... INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, so whichever ran first claimed the name and the
other silently no-opped — decided by boot order, not by any declaration.

| producer | key |
|---|---|
| `metadata-protocol`'s `ensureMetadataOverlayIndexes` (runtime, ADR-0048) | `(type, name, organization_id, COALESCE(package_id, ''))` `WHERE state = 'active'` |
| `packages/metadata`'s `addSysMetadataOverlayIndex` | `(type, name, organization_id, environment_id, scope)` |

The second is the pre-ADR-0048 key. `environment_id` was retired by ADR-0005 (2026-05
revision) — it is NULL on every new row, and SQL UNIQUE treats NULLs as DISTINCT, so that
index constrains nothing; `scope` is not in the current discriminator at all.

## The measurement that chose the direction

The issue left the fork open — delete the producer vs align its key — hinging on whether a
`DatabaseLoader` shape exists that never reaches `ensureOverlayIndex`. Both halves were
measured.

**Reachability.** `DatabaseLoader` is constructed only by `MetadataManager.setDatabaseDriver`
/ `setDataEngine`. `setDataEngine` has zero in-tree callers; `setDatabaseDriver` is
auto-called only when the manager is given both `datasource` and `driver`, which no in-tree
caller passes. `MetadataPlugin` — the only `NodeMetadataManager` constructor, and what
`standalone-stack.ts` boots — passes `{rootDir, watch, formats}` and registers no
`DatabaseLoader`. That is deliberate and documented (`packages/metadata/README.md`,
`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`: do not bridge automatically; the loader stays
available for control-plane services that opt in explicitly). `cloud` and `objectui`
reference `DatabaseLoader` zero times. So yes — a DatabaseLoader-only shape is possible, and
`ensureOverlayIndex` would never run in it.

**But "align the key" rested on a false premise**, and real SQLite says so. On a plain
`DatabaseLoader` boot the stored DDL is already:

```
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX `idx_sys_metadata_overlay_active` on `sys_metadata`
  (`type`, `name`, `organization_id`, `package_id`)
```

That is the **declared** index from `metadata-core`'s `sys-metadata.object.ts`, materialized
by `SqlDriver.syncDeclaredIndexes` — the current key, present without any help from this
package. Running the old producer against that table changed the stored DDL by nothing while
returning `status: 'created'`. Its one non-no-op window (table present, declared indexes not
yet materialized — which the engine path hits by construction, since ObjectQL's startup owns
the sync) installed the **retired** key, and `syncDeclaredIndexes` skips by name, so nothing
ever repaired it.

So the function could only ever do nothing or do harm. Both deployment shapes already have a
correctly-keyed owner: the runtime partial index from `metadata-protocol`, and — without it —
the coarser unrestricted UNIQUE from the declaration, exactly as `sys-metadata.object.ts`
documents ("the coarser fallback that a driver without that runtime migration gets").
**Deleted, not aligned.**

## Changes

- Removed `packages/metadata/src/migrations/add-sys-metadata-overlay-index.ts` and its
  barrel export, leaving a grep-findable tombstone in `migrations/index.ts` that records the
  measurement so the producer is not reintroduced.
- Removed both call sites in `DatabaseLoader.ensureSchema()`. The engine-path `catch` that
  was empty now reports per the ADR-0120 D4 shape — it names what did not happen (the
  `project_id` to `environment_id` forward migration was skipped), points at the fix, and
  never blocks the boot.

## Tests

New `overlay-index-single-producer.test.ts` asserts the **stored DDL** on real SQLite, not
the absence of an exception — the defect was never a throw, the losing producer returned
`status: 'created'` just like the winning one.

**Reverse verification, directions predicted before running.** Restoring the producer from
`origin/main`: 3 failed / 84 passed.

- **RED as predicted:** the engine-path case, the barrel-exports-no-producer case, and
  `issues NO overlay-index DDL` in `database-loader.test.ts`.
- **GREEN by design, also predicted:** the `syncSchema` cases. The declared index has already
  claimed the name with the current key before the old producer runs, so it cannot go red
  there — those cases pin the *covering* producer, which is the reason deletion is safe
  rather than merely tidy. Asserting they should go red would be fiction.
- **One prediction was wrong, and is recorded rather than reshaped:** the pre-existing-table
  case was expected red, on the theory it reaches the benign "already exists" branch with the
  declared indexes unbuilt. A real `syncSchema` does not throw there — it reconciles the
  table and builds the declared indexes anyway. That branch is reachable only with a mock
  driver, and is covered as such in `database-loader.test.ts`.

`database-loader.test.ts`'s existing case asserting the stale DDL **was** issued is flipped;
its sibling still pins that the post-sync migrations run.

Gates enumerated from `.github/workflows/lint.yml` and run in the foreground: `pnpm lint`,
`pnpm typecheck` (125/125), all 31 `check:*` gates, and `@objectstack/metadata` 578/578.
`check:engine-double-contract` went red first on the new engine double and is green after
trimming it to the read verb the test actually drives.
